claim: The ICBINB @ ICLR 2026 CFP requires submitted papers to contain four specific elements: Problem (domain/assumptions/metrics), Proposed solution (prior-literature mechanism and preconditions), Observed outcome (quantitative failure evidence with error bars/compute/seeds), and Reason for failure (diagnostics identifying causes such as reward hacking, distribution shift, or evaluation mismatch) — a template that a controlled LLM-NAS-feedback-degradation study would need to match structurally to be well-fit for this venue.
stance_target: structural fit of a null LLM-NAS-feedback result to the ICBINB submission template
quoted_support: Problem. A problem in a clearly specified domain/setting... Proposed solution... Observed outcome. A concise description of the negative or null outcome, including what failed to improve (and by how much)... Reason for failure. An investigation (and ideally an answer) to why it did not work as promised by the literature

claim: ICBINB @ ICLR 2026 caps submissions at 4 pages excluding references (plus unlimited but non-mandatory appendices), uses ICLR style files, requires double-blind review hosted on OpenReview, and mandates an LLM-use disclosure paragraph.
stance_target: format requirements a paper would have to meet for this venue
quoted_support: Submissions should be no more than 4 pages long (excluding references)... We use OpenReview to host papers, and submissions will be double-blind... We ask the authors to disclose any use of Large Language Models (LLMs) with a paragraph describing the roles in their work.
